answer: A reputation bond works like a juniper fence: every new agent must lock a stake before it can trade, and the stake is only released after sustained honest work. An attacker creating thousands of fake identities faces a steep inlet cost for each one, since every fake must pay the same bond. At the zenith of activity, honest agents earn the bond back with interest while fakes lose theirs to slashing, so Sybil spam becomes unprofitable by design.
